facts.material: natural stone (charcoal-gray to black, mottled, brown and white flecks); exact stone type not stated
facts.form: rectangular slab 115-122 in x 65-75 in, 0.75 or 1.5 in thick, top polished, sides simply sawn
facts.end_use: cut to size after importation for countertops, bathroom and office furniture surfaces

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 6802 worked monumental or building stone; chapter 68 note 2 covers all natural stone similarly worked; a polished face is worked beyond simply cut or sawn so ch. 25 (2515/2516) is excluded
GRI 6: 6802.99 other stone (assuming non-granite, non-marble/calcareous, e.g. gneiss like sibling stones); residual Other 6802.99.00.90 for polished countertop stock not cut to size

rejected_alternatives.reason: granite line; lab analysis not given, dark mottled stone more like gneiss in the parallel ruling
top is polished, more than merely cut/sawn, so chapter 25 excluded by ch. 68 note 1(a)
slabs line is for quartzite; stone not identified as quartzite

missing_facts: laboratory stone identification (granite, gneiss, quartzite or calcareous)
classification.rationale: Polished-face natural stone slabs fall under 6802 (worked building stone). The description omits the lab stone identification; the closely analogous N358799 (polished Brazilian countertop stone, gneiss) classified in 6802.99.0090 while granite went to 6802.93.0010. Assuming a non-granite stone, 6802.99.00.90.
